author: Pontoppidan, 1763
status: 나그네새 수천 마리 · 겨울철새 수백 마리
summary: 흔한 겨울철새로, 국내에서는 주로 제주도와 남해, 동해 연안에서 겨울을 나며 항만이나 연안에서 가끔 눈에 띈다. 잠수해 물고기를 잡아먹는다. 번식지에서는 호숫가 식물 한가운데를 납작하게 다져 알 2개를 낳는데, 알은 반점이 있는 올리브색에서 갈색까지 여러 가지이다. 세계적으로는 유럽, 아시아, 아메리카의 북부와 일본, 사할린, 중국, 타이완 등지에 분포한다.

art.subject: Red-throated Loon (Gavia stellata), adult in winter (non-breeding) plumage, as seen off Korean coasts from November to March: crown and hindneck pale grey; extensive white face with the eye set in white; chin, throat, foreneck and sides of the neck white; back and wings grey-brown densely sprinkled with small white spots; underparts white. Slender, pale grey bill that looks slightly upturned and is usually held tilted up; dark red eye; legs black.
art.pose: floating low on the sea, about to dive
art.scene: Korean winter coastal waters off Jeju with a gentle swell; no people, buildings or text
views: adult winter, side view swimming: pale grey crown and hindneck, white face with the eye in white, white throat and foreneck, grey-brown back densely spotted white, white underparts, slender slightly upturned pale grey bill tilted up

adult breeding, side view swimming: plain grey head and neck sides, fine black-and-white streaks on the hindneck, dark reddish-brown throat patch on the foreneck, plain dark brown back without spots, slender upturned black bill
art.build: The smallest loon, 61–67cm, larger than a Mallard but with a slender, low-lying body, small head and thin neck. Bill thin and shorter than the head, its upper edge nearly straight and the lower edge angled up so that it looks slightly upturned, typically carried tilted upward. Legs set far back near the tail. Floats low and dives for fish. In flight the neck sags slightly and the feet project beyond the short tail.
avoid: Do not paint a thick, straight, dagger-like bill; that belongs to Black-throated Loon (Gavia arctica) and Pacific Loon (Gavia pacifica).
Do not paint a dark cap reaching below the eye in winter; the face is extensively white.
Do not paint a white flank patch or bold black-and-white checkering on the back.
